newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end lower in dull trade, Astra down.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end lower in dull trade, Astra down.

text.p: Swedish shares closed lower on Friday after a quiet day's trade with falls in drugs major Astra leading the depression and the only bright spot the forestry sector.
The Stockholm general index fell 0.46 percent to 2,651.36 as shares worth 3.48 billion crowns changed hands.
"It's been a very quiet day but we have had option expiries in many shares and this has been the driving force behind S-E-Banken and Astra," one broker said.
Astra closed five crowns lower at 342.5 and pulled the drugs sector index down 0.77 percent.
Astra reports it first quarter earnings on Monday. A Reuters poll found the market expected a 14 percent rise in profit to 3.93 billion crowns.
S-E-Banken ended one crown lower at 80 crowns.
Telecoms giant Ericsson also finished lower, dipping 1.5 crowns to 250 crowns.
The forestry sector defied the negative market trend and rose 0.60 percent.
Cooperative Sodra said it was raising pulp prices to $580 a tonne from $520 and short fibre prices to 460 ecu a tonne from 400.
"We think that prices have a good chance to continue to rise," Sodra's marketing director Hans Burmeister told Reuters.
The biggest gains in the sector were posted by Stora that rose 3.5 to 101 crowns.

The bank sector closed 0.53 percent lower despite some interest in banking stocks when U.S. credit rating agency Standard & Poor's said it was raising its outlook for Sweden to stable from negative. The announcement saw debt yields fall and the crown firmed.
